out_items.name: No bare hand contact with ready-to-eat food, or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed

violations.title: No Bare Hand Contact with RTE Foods
violations.observation: Food employee(s) was observed handling the following ready-to-eat foods using their bare hands: cut limes at bar
violations.corrective_action: Except when washing fruits and vegetables, food employees may not contact ready-to-eat foods using their bare hands. Employees shall be using suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, or clean disposable gloves to handle all ready-to-eat foods. Proper handling of food and effective handwashing procedures will help prevent foodborne illness. Person in charge discarded limes and trained staff on glove use while preparing ready to eat foods.

violations.title: Shellstock Label Marked, Last Date Served/Sold Info
violations.observation: The date when the last oyster shellstock from the container is sold or served is not recorded on the tag or label.
violations.corrective_action: The identity of the source of shellstock (oysters, clams, mussels) that are sold or served shall be maintained by retaining shellstock tags or labels and marking the tag or label with the date when the last shellstock from the container is sold or served. Person in charge trained all staff on proper labeling procedures, and marked all available tags with accurate date of last use.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: smoked salmon above cooked chicken wings in prepped food walk in cooler
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. Person in charge placed all raw meat below all cooked foods.

violations.title: Before Use After Cleaning
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment were not observed sanitized: all glassware from bar dish machine.
violations.corrective_action: All utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use and after cleaning. Person in charge properly sanitized all glassware.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: cooked asparagus actively cooling in prepped food walk in cooler with cling film covering the top of containers, preventing air circulation; observed Cajun cream on back prep table with temperature ranging from 70-154F in ice bath, indicating the early start of the cooling process.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. Person in charge trained all staff members on the proper cooling processes and placed items to be cooled within their designated perimeters.

violations.observation: No records of freezing for parasite destruction are maintained for the following raw, raw marinated, partially cooked or marinated-partially cooked fish that are served or sold in ready-to-eat form: salmon fillet
violations.corrective_action: If raw or partially cooked fish are served or sold in ready-to-eat form, the person in charge shall record the freezing temperature and time to which the fish are subjected and shall retain the records for the frozen fish at the food establishment for 90 calendar days beyond the time of service or sale to a consumer. Person in charge will fully cook salmon fillet until proper parasite destruction letter has been provided to EHS.

out_items.name: Proper cooking time and temperatures

violations.title: (2017) Non-Continuous Cooking Process
violations.observation: The following raw animal foods were not properly cooked using a non-continuous cooking process: CFM SHARED THAT CHICKEN SATAY WAS COOKED TO 130F AND STORED IN VULCAN HOT HOLDING CABINET AT 118F FOR ABOUT 30 MINUTES.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods that were cooked using a non-continuous cook process shall be subject to an initial heating process that is no longer than 60 minutes in duration; immediately, after initial heating, cooled according to the time and temperature parameters specified for cooked time/temperature control for safety food; after cooling, held frozenor cold; prior to sale or service, cooked using a process that heats all parts of the food to a temperature and for a time as specified under 3-401.11A-C; Cooled according to the time and temperature parameters specified under 3-501.14A if not hot held, served immediately or held using time as a public health control. CFM DISCARDED THE CHICKEN SATAY.

violations.title: (2017) Non-Continuous Cooking Written Procedures
violations.observation: The following raw animal foods were not prepared and stored according to written procedures: THERE IS NO WRITTEN NON-CONTINUOUS COOKING PROCEDURE FOR CHICKEN SATAY.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods that were cooked using a non-continuous cook process shall be prepared and stored according to written procedures that have obtained approval from the regulatory authority, are maintained in the food establishment and are available to the regulatory authority upon request, describe hot the requirements are to be monitored and documented and corrective actions taken, describe how the foods are to be marked as foods that must be further cooked, describe how the foods are to be separated from ready-to-eat foods. THE FACILITY WILL NOT PERFORM NON-CONTINUOUS COOKING IN FUTURE.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Commercially Processed Food, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is commercially processed is not used or discarded within 24 hours of when the original container was opened and is not observed to be date marked: BLUE CHEESE (36F) AND GOUDA CHEESE (40F).
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety commercially processed foods when opened and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of the original container was opened. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. This date cannot exceed any manufacturer determined 'use-by' date based on food safety. CFM MARKED THE FOOD ITEMS WITH DATE.
